source.title: 1 Layer Induction Heads and Some Research

page_placements.theme: Architectural changes that build in or reroute induction (KV shifting, convolution, n-gram heads, value residuals)

record.file_problem: The full post text is present. Figures are referenced but their plotted images or underlying data are not included; use only the results the post states in prose or its table.
record.tranche_reason: The post reports experiments challenging and refining the claim that induction needs multiple layers: a sequential recurrent one-layer setup shows induction-like behaviour, while a parallel one-layer setup does not. It also reports further results about circuit components and training transitions.
record.gate_note: The post cites prior papers' claims, but those are not study results and are not recorded as rows. Results from Figures 2–8 are included only where the post describes an outcome in words. The HellaSwag, ARC, LAMBADA and validation-perplexity comparisons are not rows because they do not measure the induction behaviour or in-context learning named by the versions. The value-content ablation figures are difficult to assign to a particular model from the supplied table layout; see rows_left_out.
record.test_reason: The post trains its own 1-layer parallel, 1-layer sequential (recurrent) and 2-layer models on a synthetic repeated-block task. It measures induction score, second-half loss and K/Q/V corruption. It argues that induction needs two composed heads, not two layers, which restates the originals' 'not in 1-layer models' statement. Results bear on V1, V2 and V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author also argues that induction requires composition of two heads rather than two layers. He reports K-composition as dominant, suggests LayerNorm shapes how heads pass information, and concludes that OV copying is single-head while QK matching needs composition.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a synthetic repeating-block dataset and compares parallel one-layer, recurrent/sequential one-layer, and two-layer setups; also trains a No-OV model. This differs from the original training setup and is not an explicit replication of its full method.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome differs between parallel and recurrent/sequential one-layer attention and the two-layer setup. The 2-layer model has a later sharp transition, whereas the sequential model improves gradually at that point.

fits_no_version.finding: A ~110M model with no V/O projections keeps an induction bump about equal to baseline (2.715 vs 2.816). Its copy accuracy is higher (0.556 vs 0.195), and K becomes load-bearing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induction-like behaviour can be carried by alternative pathways (e.g. keys) when the OV circuit is removed.

record.problems: The evidence uses a synthetic periodic dataset and provides no stated uncertainty estimates. Most plotted results are not present in the supplied text as figures or numerical data. The post itself notes that periodicity could permit a block-size and phase inference strategy, so the dataset does not uniquely require copying from a matching earlier token.
record.rows_left_out: The table's value-content ablation figures are retained as r14–r15, but their multiplier meaning and model-column assignment are unclear. No separate rows were made for the validation perplexity, HellaSwag, ARC, or LAMBADA results because they do not measure the claim's induction or in-context-learning behaviour.

untested.parts: A bump in the overall training loss; co-occurrence with in-context learning on natural text.
All parts. The No-OV and baseline models report an undefined 'induction bump' only.
Training data and training setup were not varied; only architecture differed.
Natural-language training and other model sizes.

missing.what: QK/OV circuit analysis. All three setups show an OV copying diagonal, but the 1L parallel model lacks a QK matching diagonal and the 1L sequential model forms both.
Attention maps show a previous-token pattern in Head 0 and an induction diagonal in Head 1 for 1L sequential and 2L. Head 0 is cleaner in 1L sequential.
Early induction transition location (~10^1 M tokens), consistent across multiple seeds.

record.verdict_notes: Informal LessWrong post. It reports no uncertainty, and the figures are unavailable. A commenter notes that the periodic data permits period-inference shortcuts. The 1L sequential setup is effectively two serial attention steps, so it restates rather than refutes composition. V5 links were removed because only architecture varied. The No-OV experiment alters the architecture on purpose, and its metrics are undefined.

versions.untested_parts: The post tests synthetic repeated-block induction-like behaviour in its parallel, sequential recurrent, and two-layer setups. It does not establish the mechanism in other models or on natural language data.
The post compares induction metrics and second-half loss during training on a synthetic dataset. It does not report the claimed bump in the overall training loss curve.
The experiments do not measure most in-context learning in large transformers or loss falling with token index in few-shot tasks.
No sweep across model families, sizes, training runs, architectures beyond the described setups, or modalities is reported.
The post varies architectural setup on a synthetic dataset, but does not vary data properties or systematically test whether in-context learning persists.
The post does not test few-shot task learning or compare its mechanisms with induction heads.
The post discusses transitions in its synthetic-data experiments only; it does not test whether the same pattern holds in other training setups or models.

relationships.reason: Induction forms only where one head can read another's output (r3, r5). The parallel model fails (r2, r1). Key corruption hurts most, consistent with K-composition (r7).
relationships.display_finding: Sequential models formed induction while the parallel control failed, and corrupting keys caused the greatest damage, consistent with key composition.
